establishment.year_convention: Year 1 is the starting establishment season; a member ages by year - 1 at later numeric checkpoints. Height and weight are held at the supplied profile values because the current contract has no growth model.

establishment.arc_policy_comparison: ARC allocation is tested after the biological calculation and never constrains the planted perennial footprint or annual bridge.

planning_guideline.label: Approximately 1 ha of productive land per adult is an early ARC planning benchmark; the property/household model refines it.

allocation_methods.proportional_hectares: All allocable site-lease pools are proportional to calculated productive hectares.
allocation_methods.base_plus_hectare: Recommended: productive-land value and area-dependent tax follow productive hectares; common-property value and fixed land-holding costs are divided equally.
allocation_methods.equal_shared_and_hectare_land: Property tax and shared land-holding costs are equal; land finance recovery follows productive hectares.

sources.title: Borrowing basics - 3 ways to prepare for your next loan
sources.finding: FCC says land loans typically require 25% down, land loans can reach up to 29 years, and most are in the 20-25-year range. It distinguishes a loan term, such as 5 or 10 years, from the amortization period.
sources.evidence_status: primary lender guidance; not a binding quote or universal requirement

sources.title: Land and Buildings
sources.finding: FCC offers producer land/building financing with lender-selected interest terms, maturity dates, amortization periods and repayment schedules.
sources.evidence_status: primary lender product description; entity eligibility and pricing require underwriting

sources.title: Canadian Agricultural Loans Act Program: Before you apply
sources.finding: CALA loans are administered by lenders for eligible farmers and agricultural co-operatives. The maximum repayment term for land purchases is 15 years, although a lender may amortize longer with a balloon payment at year 15; floating and fixed rate caps are defined relative to lender rates.
sources.evidence_status: government program rule; eligibility for an ARC land-holding entity must be confirmed

sources.title: Deteriorating farmland affordability presents challenges
sources.finding: FCC uses 25% down and 25-year amortization as an analytical farmland-purchase assumption.
sources.evidence_status: primary lender analytical convention; not a product promise

interpretation.down_payment: 25% is the best-supported neutral planning case found; actual equity, collateral and lender policy may differ.
interpretation.amortization: 20-25 years is the neutral planning band in FCC guidance. A 30-year amortization is possible in some land products but is not established here for an ARC land-holding entity.
interpretation.loan_term: Loan term/renewal is separate from amortization. The project must refinance or renew at the term end unless it has an open or fully amortizing structure.
interpretation.interest_rate: No current public lender quote was found for this specific entity and security structure. Use lender-quoted rates or explicit sensitivity cases, not a canonical expected rate.
interpretation.eligibility: The ARC entity must be assessed as an agricultural producer/co-operative, commercial borrower, land trust/non-profit or another eligible borrower; residential mortgage assumptions do not establish eligibility.

land_insurance.notes: Property and liability premiums depend on buildings, contents, activities, visitors, location, limits and risk. The CAD 3,000 input is a working planning allowance, not an insurance quote.

land_market.planning_curve_basis: The 5–10 ha value is anchored to the 2024 Grey County survey benchmark converted from CAD 19,000 per tillable acre. Other values remain explicit fallback sensitivities and are not used when a parcel-size band has sufficient local observations.
notes: Survey benchmarks per tillable acre are not silently treated as whole-parcel sale prices.
Vacant-land bands exclude substantial buildings while retaining minor improvements as explicitly flagged observations when they are not a separate material asset.
Improved properties enter gross acquisition statistics at their actual whole-property asking or sale price; no farmhouse or barn value is silently subtracted.
Existing improvements expose candidate ARC reuse assets, but no monetary capital offset is applied without condition, legal and replacement-cost evidence.
The importer accepts manually verified lawful observations; no REALTOR.ca scraping is used.

market_band_crossover.explanation: The internal two-adult scan first enters the measured 20–40 ha band at 22 adults (20.06 ha) for the vacant_land view. The observed land-price change is -$25661.89/ha per hectare; the household charge changes by -$268.96/month.

economic_sweet_spot.explanation: Within the measured 20–40 ha band, the first two-adult step with no more than 15% additional per-household savings is 22 to 24 adults: $4.45 per household, or 1.6%. This is a provisional economic sweet spot, not an optimization result.

economic_crossover.explanation: The market-band crossover occurs at 22 adults in the internal scan for the vacant_land view. The provisional economic sweet spot begins at 22 adults because the next two-adult step saves only 1.6%. The 20–40 ha band has 4 observations and the 40+ ha band is unresolved for this view.

market_band_crossover.explanation: No transition into a lower-priced evidence-backed parcel band is currently supported for the improved_property view.

improved_property.explanation: No adult-scale case currently enters a lower-priced parcel band with sufficient measured whole-property evidence for the improved_property view.

market_band_crossover.explanation: The internal two-adult scan first enters the measured 20–40 ha band at 22 adults (20.06 ha) for the arc_usable_acquisition view. The observed land-price change is -$25661.89/ha per hectare; the household charge changes by -$268.96/month.

economic_sweet_spot.explanation: Within the measured 20–40 ha band, the first two-adult step with no more than 15% additional per-household savings is 22 to 24 adults: $4.45 per household, or 1.6%. This is a provisional economic sweet spot, not an optimization result.

arc_usable_acquisition.explanation: The market-band crossover occurs at 22 adults in the internal scan for the arc_usable_acquisition view. The provisional economic sweet spot begins at 22 adults because the next two-adult step saves only 1.6%. The 20–40 ha band has 4 observations and the 40+ ha band is supported for this view.

notes: Adult count is the primary settlement-scale variable. Household and dwelling count is a resulting planning arrangement.
Except for the 1-adult case, each pair of adults is stress-tested as a two-adult household capable of supporting three dependent children.
The family-capacity case is not a forecast of actual ARC demographics.
The public scale table includes 1, 4, 12, 16, 20, 22, 24, 28, 40 and 56 adults. The internal crossover scan remains 1 adult plus every even count through 56.

Vacant-land, improved-property and all ARC-usable acquisition views remain separate. Improved properties use their gross whole-property price; no farmhouse, barn or servicing value is silently deducted.
Land price bands use measured listing observations where the minimum sample threshold is met. Sparse bands remain unresolved rather than being filled from the planning sensitivity curve.

The economic crossover is a bounded demonstration result. It does not establish a universal Grey County price curve, and improved-property condition, recreational premiums and asking-versus-sale differences remain material caveats.

land_accounting.accounting_rule: Annual food, perennial food, on-property feed and woody heating are exclusive productive zones. The emergency/rotation reserve is retained as a conservative exclusive reserve. Soil/water, wildlife, fibre and habitat functions are hosted within perennial/woody zones and are reported as overlapping multifunctional coverage, not added hectares. Market production first uses annual land released during the handoff; only the remainder is additional site area.

component_classification.emergency_resilience_reserve: exclusive land requirement in the central robust case; can be reduced if reserve production is demonstrably carried inside the food zones
component_classification.soil_water_management: overlaps perennial food and woody heating zones; already inherent where those zones are designed with continuous roots and runoff interception
component_classification.wildlife_protection: overlaps woody/perennial edge; not a separate hectare block in the central accounting
component_classification.paths_access: not separately allocated; paths are assumed to pass through productive zones
component_classification.greenhouse_building: not included in this land total; any greenhouse footprint must be added from a site plan
component_classification.fibre_material_production: no separate hectare; can use coppice and released annual/perennial land
component_classification.market_export_production: optional policy/design allowance; first uses released annual acreage and only the residual is additional
component_classification.habitat_biodiversity: overlaps perennial/woody zones; no separate hectare added

recurring_labour.labour_objective_note: Physically demanding hours include annual soil preparation, planting, weeding, annual harvest, coppice cutting, firewood hauling and splitting. Light/moderate hours include perennial pruning, food harvest, irrigation, orchard and wildlife work. Processing/storage includes food preservation, nut drying/shelling/storage and firewood stacking/drying. Greenhouse labour is zero because no greenhouse footprint is allocated in this mature land row.

mature_rows.evidence_boundary: Livestock modules are optional illustrative household units, not ARC requirements. Feed conversion, output, feed-area yield and labour are modelled planning assumptions bounded by the cited extension guidance.
mature_rows.selection_rule: lowest tested share meeting >=70% annual-cultivation reduction, >=20% annual plant-food resilience share, and protein/fat screening thresholds; land deficit remains an output.

heating.source: ECCC Owen Sound 1981-2010 HDD plus explicit geometry/envelope assumptions
heating.audit: All geometry and envelope values are user/design/modelling assumptions except the ECCC HDD normal; no as-built measurement was available.
model_notes: Building heating is calculated from form geometry, floor area, RSI envelope values, window loss, ventilation/infiltration, ECCC HDD, indoor temperature, heater efficiency and thermal bridges.
Building presets are transparent physical assumptions, not as-built surveys.

rabbit_meat.label: Self-replacing rabbits
rabbit_meat.unit_label: Breeding does/buck plus household fryer output
rabbit_meat.notes: Breeding stock, replacements and fryer output are included in the self-replacing household rabbitry. Forage and leaves are bounded supplements rather than an assumption of grass-only production.

chicken_eggs.label: Self-replacing dual-purpose chicken flock
chicken_eggs.unit_label: 8 breeding hens plus 1 breeding rooster; integrated eggs and surplus-bird meat

reproduction.reproduction_mode_note: Broody hens avoid incubator electricity but reduce edible eggs; a locally powered incubator trades electricity and labour for more controlled hatch timing.
reproduction.genetic_resilience_note: Occasional unrelated breeding-stock introduction may be prudent, but it is not an annual production input.
reproduction.evidence_status: planning synthesis; breed and reproduction figures require local flock validation

chicken_eggs.notes: Canonical chicken is an integrated, naturally mating, true-breeding dual-purpose flock. Gross eggs are reduced for incubation and losses; meat comes from surplus cockerels and cull birds. Feed includes breeding adults and growing replacements.

chicken_meat.label: Fast-growing meat chicken sensitivity
chicken_meat.notes: Non-canonical sensitivity only. It assumes recurring production birds and cannot qualify as ARC self-replacing carrying capacity.

goose_meat.label: Self-replacing grazing-biased geese
goose_meat.unit_label: Breeding geese plus surplus gosling meat
goose_meat.notes: Pasture contribution is substantial but seasonal; breeding adults, replacement birds, winter feed, shelter and water are included.

goat_meat.label: Self-replacing browse-biased goats
goat_meat.unit_label: Breeding does/buck plus annual meat-kid output

reproduction.evidence_status: bounded smallholder planning synthesis; goat food composition profile unresolved

goat_meat.notes: Goats can browse a large share of their diet, but browse inventory, fencing, hay and winter supplementation are site-specific. A matching CNF goat-meat food form remains unresolved for micronutrient accounting.

chantecler.label: Chantecler
chantecler.forage_behaviour: outdoor forage contribution is plausible but not quantified here
chantecler.locomotion: mobile enough for outdoor ranging; flock-specific validation required
chantecler.heat_tolerance: not quantified; Grey County cold hardiness is the relevant reference condition
chantecler.growth_rate: slow-growing dual-purpose reference; not a broiler performance claim
chantecler.feed_requirement: bounded flock synthesis; lower-concentration assumption than industrial broiler
chantecler.evidence_status: qualitative breed/reference evidence; quantitative flock values are planning synthesis

plymouth_rock.label: Plymouth Rock
plymouth_rock.forage_behaviour: outdoor-range candidate; no local intake estimate

rhode_island_red.label: Rhode Island Red
rhode_island_red.forage_behaviour: outdoor-range candidate; no local intake estimate

sussex.label: Sussex
sussex.forage_behaviour: good outdoor-range candidate; no local intake estimate

canonical.label: Self-replacing true-breeding dual-purpose flock
canonical.breeding: natural mating with retained replacement birds; no recurring chicks or pullets
canonical.locomotion_and_range: outdoor mobility, range use and forage behaviour are relevant; intake contribution remains bounded and site-specific
canonical.heat_tolerance: not a Grey County selection driver and not quantitatively modelled
canonical.growth_and_feed: slow-growing/dual-purpose planning boundary; no commercial broiler feed-conversion or carcass assumptions are inherited
canonical.climate: cold-hardy reference range for Grey County, with Chantecler selected as the conservative reference
canonical.evidence_status: breed comparison and flock outputs are planning synthesis; local flock validation required

industrial_sensitivity.label: Fast-growing commercial broiler sensitivity
industrial_sensitivity.breeding: recurring production-bird replacement; excluded from canonical ARC carrying capacity
industrial_sensitivity.locomotion_and_range: selection for rapid growth can reduce mobility/range suitability relative to slower-growing birds
industrial_sensitivity.heat_tolerance: comparative heat/locomotion evidence is context-specific and not transferred into the canonical flock
industrial_sensitivity.growth_and_feed: commercial performance is a separate sensitivity and must not be used for the canonical flock
industrial_sensitivity.climate: not selected as the Grey County self-replacing reference

conventional_reference.label: External-feed sensitivity (non-ARC)
conventional_reference.description: Normal smallholder reference ration with external feed; shown only as a sensitivity and excluded from canonical ARC optimization.

low_food_competition.label: Low-food-competition sensitivity (non-ARC)
low_food_competition.description: Maximizes forage, browse, culls and residues while retaining external supplements; not ARC feed self-sufficiency compliant.

arc_integrated.label: ARC on-site feed
arc_integrated.description: All dietary feed energy and protein is produced on the ARC property through finite co-products and dedicated feed hectares. Purchased feed is prohibited.

property_feed_supply_rules.status: explicit planning synthesis; requires a property biomass inventory before operational use
property_feed_supply_rules.double_counting_rule: These are finite co-products/overlays within the modeled food areas. Dedicated feed hectares are added for any shortfall; the same stream is not assigned twice.

members.label: Representative adult woman
members.status: official Health Canada DRI total-protein reference; food quality and amino-acid adequacy remain separate checks

quality_reference.method: PDCAAS reference amino-acid pattern; a complete digestibility score is not assigned without food-specific amino-acid evidence.

protein_demand.caveat: Total protein RDA is a screening requirement. This output does not prove indispensable-amino-acid adequacy, digestibility, micronutrients or food safety.

macro_range_check.status: screening check only; does not establish micronutrient sufficiency

assumptions.macro_energy_factors: 0.016736 GJ/kg protein and carbohydrate; 0.037656 GJ/kg fat

property_supply.source: explicit planning synthesis; requires a property biomass inventory before operational use
property_supply.double_counting_rule: These are finite co-products/overlays within the modeled food areas. Dedicated feed hectares are added for any shortfall; the same stream is not assigned twice.

central_mix.name: four-function perennial food mix
central_mix.composition: 25% early berry/vitamin layer; 25% hazelnut fat/protein layer; 25% chestnut starch layer; 25% fruit/storage layer

evidence_limitations: No replicated, long-term, near-zero-input perennial food-forest yield trial for ordinary Grey-Bruce land was located.
Ontario hazelnut guidance explicitly says the province has no established hazelnut yield history; the central 0.75 t/ha value is an unvalidated conservative synthesis.
Chestnut bearing-time evidence is regionally relevant but yield evidence is mainly outside Ontario; chestnut suitability, blight, frost and wildlife risk remain unresolved.
Heartnut and oak/acorn functions are documented but excluded from the central food energy mix because no defensible Grey-Bruce yield series was found.
The curves are bounded interpolations between published bearing-time anchors and planning milestones, not annual field measurements.

methodology.labour_note: Metabolic food demand and explicit assigned labour capacity are separate inputs. Sex, age, height, weight and activity do not infer agricultural capability.
methodology.household_land_role_note: Members under 18 are dependent children by default. Children add pooled food demand while dependent, but do not add permanent perennial acreage to the parental parcel; after transition their adult allocation is outside this calculation. Year 1 is the starting establishment season; a member ages by year - 1 at later numeric checkpoints. Height and weight are held at the supplied profile values because the current contract has no growth model.
methodology.land_accounting: Annual food, perennial food, heating and exclusive reserve are kept distinct; soil/water, wildlife, fibre and habitat functions are reported as overlapping multifunctional coverage.
methodology.custom_household_note: The browser imports pure canonical EER, pooled household-demand, balanced-food, building-heating and labour-capacity functions. Custom transition charts use the same adult/dependent demand profile as the CLI model; household presets display full canonical transition rows.
methodology.external_input_note: Energy-condition multipliers are regional scenario overlays, not replacements for the biological carrying-capacity evidence model.
